meta.battery: Model-comparison cycle: seeded-random variable battery (env, labels, policies, concurrency, fleet drift) run under a specific model.
meta.title: Model comparison B: gpt-6.1-sol runs the variable battery

results.title: Random compute in exec
results.prose: I asked the sandbox to multiply 9027 by 5792 and got exactly 52284384 back. This checks that exec returns the expected output for a real command, rather than treating a successful RPC alone as proof of useful work.

results.title: Random policy subset
results.prose: I created a sandbox whose sampled policy contained one API endpoint, then confirmed that endpoint appeared in the stored response and github.com did not. This is a configuration round-trip check, not proof that network enforcement allowed or blocked any request; the script never exercised traffic.
steps: Sample k random endpoints from host pool
CreateSandbox with networkPolicies allowing exactly those for curl
GetSandbox: verify stored spec has exactly those hosts, no extras

results.title: Fleet snapshot + drift
results.desc: Gateway fleet stats vs previous cycle
results.prose: I compared the fleet snapshot with the previous saved snapshot: 36 gateways across seven versions, with no drift reported by the script. That gives us a useful continuity check, although this detector does not comprehensively track added or removed version keys.

results.title: Random payload FS roundtrip
results.desc: Write and re-read random hash within session
results.prose: I wrote a hash payload beginning ac80c6b95ff7 into the sandbox and checked it both immediately and through another exec call. Both reads matched, showing continuity within this sandbox lifetime—not persistence across a stop/start.
steps: ExecSandbox: write hash to /tmp/p, read back
Second ExecSandbox: read /tmp/p again — both reads match

results.title: Model self-report
results.desc: Execution provenance and approach; not a platform test.
results.detail: Executed under gpt-6.1-sol (custom-api-enmaas-devshift-net/gpt-6.1-sol). I checked the test implementation as well as its result values, separating configuration checks from enforcement claims.
results.prose: I ran this cycle under gpt-6.1-sol and checked what the harness actually asserted before writing these notes. In particular, I limited the policy finding to stored configuration and the filesystem finding to one sandbox lifetime; those boundaries matter more than making four green results sound broader than they are.
steps: (meta entry) record which model executed the run and its approach
